reuse.why: All providers reuse the shared link guards and bank lookup, but takeover repeats ownership lookup and unlink cleanup, while Fintegra copies the existing linking workflow.

duplication.why: The change duplicates four substantial blocks: ownership lookup, local unlink cleanup, account linking orchestration, and transaction download plumbing.

placement.why: Link policies, request handlers, provider downloads, configuration, and model types all reside in the established modules and layers.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on the requested linking rules, takeover option, and Fintegra integration.

maintainability.why: Shared guards make the new policies discoverable, but duplicated ownership queries and unlink field lists create multiple definitions that maintainers must keep aligned.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six linking handlers call the shared guards and findOrCreateBank; the existing unlinkAccount also disconnects providers, so it is not directly reusable for takeover.

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions reshapes the existing provider download logic with a direct response projection, and prepareAccountLink embeds the ownership query already contained in assertAccountNotLinked.

abstraction_drift.where: The shared link preparation interface gains replaceExistingLink and a takeover branch that repeats the ownership lookup; all provider linking handlers still route through the shared preparation.
